findings.title: The capture still does not filter NODE_TEST_* from its children, but the falsely-green path it opened is now closed downstream
findings.description: Carried from iteration 2 and not addressed by the iteration-3 fixes. `execFileSync('npx', ['tsx','--test',file], {cwd, encoding, stdio, timeout})` passes no `env`, so if the capture is ever run from inside a `node --test` process its children inherit NODE_TEST_CONTEXT, node's recursion guard prints only `skipping running files` and exits 0 having run nothing. CLAUDE.md records this exact trap in this repository and records `admission-gate.test.mjs:62` fixing it with an env filter. Downgraded from MEDIUM to LOW because FND-102's fix now catches the consequence: such a child produces no summary, parseFileSummary returns null, perFileCounts records null, and the diff refuses with GATE UNUSABLE ('printed no parseable node:test summary'). The residual is that the capture itself still exits 0 and prints 'no summary N' without failing, so the operator learns about it one step later than they could.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass `env: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(process.env).filter(([k]) => !k.startsWith('NODE_TEST_')))` on the execFileSync at :120, and exit non-zero from main() when `unparsed > 0`.

acceptance_criteria.evidence: StorePublishCrossInstance.test.ts:84 — two independently constructed instances on one data file, both publishes resolve. Structurally guaranteed by privateTempPath(): no two calls can name the same temp path.

StorePublishCrossInstance.test.ts:120 — a peer overwrite interposed on the SHARED temp path between write and rename; the destination still holds this publish's document, because the publish never used that path.
StorePublishCrossInstance.test.ts:161 — the shorter-over-longer overlay that produced the measured 13-15% torn publishes leaves no foreign tail.

StorePublishCrossInstance.test.ts:227 plus atomicStoreWrite.ts:209-215 — the cleanup loop iterates ownedTemps only, which contains nothing a peer could be using. releaseOwnedTemp() (atomicStoreWrite.ts:118-123) removes by value rather than by position, so a published .bak is never a candidate for a later unlink.

atomicStoreWrite.ts:35,45,93-111 — TRANSIENT_RENAME_CODES = {EPERM, EACCES, EBUSY}, RENAME_RETRY_WAITS_MS = [10,20,40,80], one initial attempt plus four retries, exhausted budget rethrows the last error leaving the destination as it was. atomicStoreWrite.test.ts:91,107,150 assert the exact wait schedule through the injected delay seam (not a wall-clock tolerance), the five-attempt exhaustion with the destination intact and parseable, and no temp left behind.
atomicStoreWrite.ts:105 — a code outside the transient set throws immediately. atomicStoreWrite.test.ts:131 asserts ENOSPC rejects on attempt one with zero recorded waits.

atomicStoreWrite.ts:169-184 — the backup goes through its own private temp plus renameWithRetry, so it is published atomically and a peer overlay on the shared .bak path cannot leave a torn backup. StorePublishCrossInstance.test.ts:269 drives the interposed different-length overlay the criterion specifies; the AC-8 table additionally asserts, per backup-writing store, that the backup parses AND equals the document the destination held immediately before the publish replaced it. The iteration-1 change making the backup best-effort does not weaken AC-7: on backup failure the previous .bak is left whole and stale (or absent), never torn, and three new cases at atomicStoreWrite.test.ts:194/226/259 pin that the primary publish still completes and that a successfully published backup survives a later primary failure.

StorePublishCrossInstance.test.ts:455 asserts stores.length === 7 and, per store, that a peer overlay on the shared temp path does not affect what is published (which is what proves the store uses a private path), plus the backup content for the five that keep one and its ABSENCE for the two that never had one. :562 asserts per store that the pre-existing error type still reaches the caller (AppError + ErrorCode, or the raw EIO by code and message) and that a failed publish leaves the destination as it was. grep confirms all seven call sites route through publishStoreAtomically and that no `.tmp` / copyFile / bare fs.rename publish path survives in any of the seven services. Note on method: the suite argues AC-1..AC-7 per store structurally — all seven go through one helper, and each row proves the helper is actually the path taken — rather than re-running all seven criteria seven times. That is a sound argument and I accept it.

StorePublishCrossInstance.test.ts:650 — two overlapping publishes through one instance, each caller's own change readable after its call resolves. REL-BGSTAB-020's in-process promise chain is untouched: the helper is called from inside each store's existing flush, and the mutation chains at e.g. AgentLifecycleService.ts:118-122 are unchanged.

concerns: AgentLifecycleService previously wrote its store with the default file mode; it now inherits the helper's 0o600 default. That matches the mode the other four stores already used explicitly and is a tightening, not a regression — but it is a mode change to agent-command-profiles.json that no acceptance criterion names. It predates this round's diff.

The backup-is-best-effort decision (iteration 1) is a deliberate behaviour choice justified by the pre-existing `try { copyFile } catch {}` contract. It is now documented at atomicStoreWrite.ts:135-137 and 171-181, warns at console.warn with destination, errno and message, and is covered by three tests. I agree with the choice and with how it is recorded.
